fields.label: Q1. What is your business name, and what does it do?
fields.value: Cedar & Vine Property Management. We manage 85 residential rental units for private landlords across one metro area, handling leasing, rent collection, maintenance coordination, and owner reporting.

fields.label: Q2. How many people work in the business, and what are their main roles?
fields.value: Owner/property manager (1, that's me), leasing & tenant coordinator (1), part-time bookkeeper (1, ~15 hrs/week).

fields.label: Q3. What is the rough fully-loaded hourly cost of each role?
Q4. Walk us through a typical week. Where does the most time get spent on work that feels repetitive, manual, or low-value?
fields.value: Re-typing maintenance requests that come in by phone, text, and email into AppFolio; chasing tenants for late rent every month; copying new applicant details into a spreadsheet and then again into the screening portal; putting together monthly owner statements by hand.

fields.label: Q5. What tasks get done over and over in almost exactly the same way?
fields.value: Sending the same move-in packet and welcome email to every new tenant; posting each vacancy to the same 4 listing sites; sending the same three late-rent reminder messages on the same schedule every month.

fields.label: Q6. Where do you or your team copy and paste information between systems, or re-enter the same data twice?
fields.value: Applicant info from our web application form gets keyed into AppFolio and again into the TransUnion SmartMove screening portal. Maintenance details get re-typed from voicemails/texts into AppFolio.

fields.label: Q7. What software, tools, and apps do you use to run the business?
fields.value: AppFolio, Gmail, Google Sheets, QuickBooks Online, DocuSign, a Google Voice number for tenant texts, Zillow Rental Manager, and TransUnion SmartMove for screening.

fields.label: Q8. For your busiest recurring tasks, roughly how often do they happen and in what volume?
fields.value: About 35 maintenance requests per month; roughly 12 rental applications per month; monthly rent reminders to ~85 tenants; about 6 new tenant onboardings per month; 20 owner statements assembled monthly.

fields.label: Q9. How do customers, clients, or leads first reach you, and how do you respond?
fields.value: Prospective tenants call or submit a Zillow inquiry; the coordinator usually replies within a day to schedule a showing and email an application link. Landlords come mostly by referral.

fields.label: Q10. What follow-ups, reminders, or nudges does someone have to remember to send?
fields.value: Rent reminders 3 days before it's due; following up with applicants who started but didn't finish the application; nudging our two maintenance vendors for their invoices; reminding tenants when a lease renewal is 60 days out.

fields.label: Q11. What scheduling or coordination back-and-forth eats time?
fields.value: Coordinating maintenance vendor visits around tenant availability usually takes 4-5 text messages per request. Scheduling showings is a few back-and-forth emails each.

fields.label: Q12. What reports, summaries, or updates do you prepare regularly, and for whom?
fields.value: Monthly owner statements pulled together from QuickBooks and AppFolio for each landlord; a weekly vacancy and delinquency summary I build in a spreadsheet for myself.

fields.label: Q13. What's currently holding the business back from growing, or what would you do with the time if you got it back?
fields.value: I can't take on more units without hiring, because admin already maxes out the three of us. I'd rather spend the time on landlord relationships and bringing on new doors.

fields.label: Q14. Have you tried to automate or streamline anything before? What happened?
fields.value: Set up a Zapier zap once to post listings, but it kept duplicating them so we turned it off. AppFolio has some built-in reminders we use but they're rigid.

fields.label: Q15. What should we NOT try to automate — the work that must stay human?
fields.value: Handling an upset tenant or any eviction conversation always needs a real person. And the final decision on who we approve to rent to stays with me.
